newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wants to avoid grain export refunds in new era.
newsitem.headline: EU wants to avoid grain export refunds in new era.

text.p: The European Union will maintain the option to use grain export subsidies in its planned farm reform but does not expect to have to use them, a senior agriculture official said on Monday.

European Commission agriculture director-general Guy Legras said EU projections suggested export refunds would not be necessary after a 20 percent cut in intervention support prices planned for the year 2000.
"We will keep the mechanism but we hope it won't have to be used," Legras said while briefing journalists in Paris on the reform plan labelled Agenda 2000.

The European Commission proposes to cut grain intervention prices to 95.35 Ecus per tonne from the current 119.19 Ecus to help prepare the 15-nation EU for expansion eastwards and a new round of global farm trade negotiations due to start in 1999.
Export subsidies are expected to be a focal point for attack by the United States and other leading grain producers in the talks on a successor pact to the 1994 Uruguay Round.
